question: US ceasefire against Iran continues through August 31?
research:
**Note up front:** Some search results contained material dated after 2026-08-24. I left all of it out, as instructed.

## 1. Resolution source
- The criteria give no URL. Resolution depends on official US and Iranian government and military statements plus a consensus of credible reporting, such as CENTCOM releases and major outlets.
- 2026-08-24: I found no reports from credible sources of a qualifying US air or missile strike on Iranian territory between August 1 and August 24. I could not reach some live blogs (Al Jazeera, Wikipedia) because the proxy refused the connection.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing that settles the question has happened as of 2026-08-24. The market resolves "No" only if a qualifying US strike lands on Iranian territory between now and August 31. My search of August 1 to 24 found no such strike, but because some sources were unreachable I can't completely rule one out.
- 2026-08-17: The 60-day Islamabad memorandum period ended with no deal. Trump said "No" when asked whether he would extend the ceasefire, and said he is "not in a hurry" to make a deal. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/17/us-iran-war-trump-hormuz.html), [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/17/us-iran-memorandum-of-understanding-expires-how-and-why-it-fell-apart)
- 2026-08-17: Reporting said there was no sign the expiry itself would trigger more US strikes. [NewsNation](https://www.newsnationnow.com/world/us-iran-war-memorandum-of-understanding/)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-24: Treasury began "Operation Economic Outcast," a set of sweeping secondary sanctions on Iranian oil. One report said the measures stopped short of the most sweeping options, and oil prices fell after Bessent spoke. [Al Jazeera live](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2026/8/24/iran-war-live-iranian-assembly-advances-plans-for-hormuz-service-fees), [Ynet](https://www.ynetnews.com/article/bjnrehcwmg)
- 2026-08-23/24: Bessent called it an "economic D-Day" and warned Trump would "respond swiftly and decisively" if Iran answered militarily. Iran's Mohsen Rezaei said any country joining the campaign would be treated as committing an act of war, and threatened to halt all Gulf oil exports. Iran's parliament moved ahead with plans for Hormuz service fees. [CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2026/08/23/world/live-news/iran-war-trump), [Asharq Al-Awsat](https://english.aawsat.com/node/5310383)
- Around 2026-08-23: Iran's president defended the memorandum as the best path forward. Trump said Iran is "not ready to make the right deal." [CBS](https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-trump-economic-crackdown/)
- 2026-08-12: Middle East Monitor, citing Pakistani sources, reported the two sides had agreed to extend the ceasefire. The White House's August 17 refusal superseded this. [MEMO](https://www.middleeastmonitor.com/20260812-us-iran-agree-to-extend-60-day-ceasefire-ahead-of-aug-17-deadline/)
- 2026-08-01/02: Trump called off a planned large attack on Iranian energy infrastructure, citing agreed "perimeters of a deal," and conditioned the pause on reaching a deal quickly. Iran denied any talks were taking place. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/02/trump-planned-attack-on-iran-canceled-after-reaching-outline-of-deal.html), [NPR](https://www.npr.org/2026/08/03/nx-s1-5917167/trump-calls-off-strike-against-iran-says-a-deal-is-close)
- 2026-07-29: CENTCOM struck dozens of IRGC targets in Iran, including Qeshm Island, after Iranian ballistic missiles were fired at US forces in Jordan. This is the last US strike on Iran I could confirm. [Al-Monitor](https://al-monitor.com/originals/2026/07/us-carries-out-strikes-southern-iran-after-irgc-attack-jordan-airbase), [Business Today](https://www.businesstoday.in/world/story/brief-pause-ends-us-hits-iran-again-after-ballistic-missile-attack-on-american-troops-in-jordan-546124-2026-07-30)

## 4. Base rates
- The war began in late February 2026. Since then the US has repeatedly paused strikes and then resumed them:
  - May 7: strikes.
  - May 27: strikes resumed after talks faltered.
  - June 17: the memorandum was signed.
  - July 7-8: it collapsed, and Trump declared it "over."
  - July: about two weeks of nightly strikes around Hormuz.
  - July 29: retaliatory strikes. [PBS](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/trump-frequently-announces-hes-halting-strikes-in-iran-but-they-keep-happening), [Wikipedia: 7 May strikes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/7_May_2026_United_States_strikes_on_Iran)
- ABC counted seven times Trump threatened devastating strikes and then didn't carry them out. [ABC](https://www-cdn.abcnews.com/Politics/7-times-trump-hed-launch-devastating-strikes-iran/story?id=135331621)
- As of August 24, there have been about 25 days with no confirmed US strike. Recent strikes have often come in response to Iranian attacks on US forces, for example the July 29 strikes after the Jordan missile attack.

[PredictMarketCap](https://predictmarketcap.com/events/us-ceasefire-against-iran-continues-throughptptpt), [Polymarket Iran hub](https://polymarket.com/iran/trump-iran)

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- The rollout of the sanctions campaign, and whether Iran follows through on its threats to cut off Hormuz or Gulf oil, or to strike countries that comply with the sanctions. Bessent has warned of a swift US military response.
- Any IRGC attack on US forces or bases, such as in Jordan, or any mining of Hormuz. These have been the recent triggers for US retaliatory strikes.
- Ongoing indirect mediation through Pakistan, Oman and Jordan, and Trump's statements on whether to extend the ceasefire or resume strikes.
- The 3-day dispute window: if an attribution is contested near August 31, resolution could be delayed.
